newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie to lose European parliament seat.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie to lose European parliament seat.

text.p: Charismatic ex-businessman and soccer boss Bernard Tapie, already ejected from the French National Assembly, will now lose his seat in the European parliament, the foreign ministry said on Thursday.

Tapie cannot keep the European seat for the same reason he was thrown out of France's parliament -- because a French court has ruled he is bankrupt and thus ineligible for public office, ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
Under European Union law, eligibility for the European parliament is determined by the laws of individual member states, Rummelhardt told a regular ministry briefing.

"This decision (to eject him) must be transmitted to the president of the European Parliament (Klaus Haensch of Germany), which has not yet been done," Rummelhardt added. He did not say when this would happen.

The flamboyant Tapie, target of a blizzard of legal actions over his now-destroyed business empire and the Marseille soccer team he once ran, had come to the ministry earlier in the day to plead that he be allowed to remain a European deputy.

After losing his parliamentary immunity in France, he faces prison since two appeal courts have confirmed jail sentences of eight and six months against him for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match. He is appealing both cases to the Supreme Court.
Tapie, a member of the small Radical Socialist party, was first elected to the French parliament in 1989 as deputy from the Bouches du Rhone department in southern France. He was re-elected in 1993.
In a new career move, he recently starred in "Men, Women: Instructions for Use", a film by French director Claude Lelouche.
